# Test fixtures

## `AndroidManifest-min.bin`

A minimal, hand-crafted **Android binary XML** (`AXML`) manifest used by the `src/apk/`
unit tests. It is *not* a real Roblox manifest and contains no copyrighted content — it
encodes a synthetic app:

```xml
<manifest package="com.example.app" xmlns:android="…">
  <uses-sdk android:minSdkVersion="26" android:targetSdkVersion="35"/>
  <application android:largeHeap="true">
    <activity android:name=".MainActivity"/>            <!-- no filter (launcher negative case) -->
    <activity android:name=".SplashActivity">
      <intent-filter>
        <action   android:name="android.intent.action.MAIN"/>
        <category android:name="android.intent.category.LAUNCHER"/>
      </intent-filter>
    </activity>
  </application>
</manifest>
```

It lets the manifest tests run with **no network and no 215 MB APK**: the tests build a tiny
in-memory zip containing this file plus crafted `lib/<abi>/…` entries.

These bytes use a **UTF-8** string pool (`UTF8_FLAG` set); the real Roblox manifest uses
UTF-16, so between this fixture and the real-APK dev validation the reader's *both* encoding
paths are exercised.

**Provenance (2026-06-04):** originally generated by a one-shot, self-validating Rust program
that emits the binary AXML by hand and re-parses it, asserting every field the tests check.
The generator is intentionally not committed — only its validated output is. 2026-06-04: the
`apk` module replaced its `axmldecoder 0.3` dependency with Eclipse's own pure-Rust, total
reader (`src/apk/axml.rs`); these committed bytes parse unchanged under the new reader (the
`apk` unit tests assert the documented fields), so no regeneration was needed.

## `AndroidManifest-utf16.bin`

The **same logical manifest** as `AndroidManifest-min.bin` but encoded with a **UTF-16**
string pool (`UTF8_FLAG` cleared) instead of UTF-8. aapt2/bundletool — and the real Roblox
manifest — emit UTF-16 pools, so this fixture drives the reader's `decode_utf16` path on good
input (`manifest_parses_utf16_string_pool` asserts it parses to the identical fields as the
UTF-8 fixture) and as one of the two bases in the totality fuzz
(`reader_is_total_under_truncation_and_mutation`). Without it, the production string-pool
decoder would never be exercised by a committed regression guard.

**Provenance (2026-06-04):** same self-validating emit-then-reparse generator approach as
`AndroidManifest-min.bin`; only the validated output is committed. Parses under Eclipse's own
reader (`src/apk/axml.rs`) to `package=com.example.app`, `.SplashActivity` launcher,
min=26 / target=35, `largeHeap=true`.

## `AndroidManifest-absent.bin`

A second hand-crafted AXML manifest that **omits `<uses-sdk>` and `android:largeHeap`**, so
the `apk` tests can pin the documented default paths: `min_sdk`/`target_sdk` are `None` (never
fabricated) and `large_heap` is `false`. It encodes `package=com.example.app`, an
`<application>` with no attributes, and a `.SplashActivity` reached via a MAIN/LAUNCHER filter.

**Provenance (2026-06-04):** same self-validating generator approach as
`AndroidManifest-min.bin`; only the validated output is committed. Parses unchanged under
Eclipse's own reader (`src/apk/axml.rs`).

## `AndroidManifest-panic.bin`

A structurally valid AXML whose single attribute carries an **invalid resource value-type
byte**. This exact input made the former `axmldecoder 0.3` dependency *panic* internally
(`unwrap`/`assert_eq!`), which under the release `panic = "abort"` profile would abort the
whole process. It is the **root-cause regression fixture**: the `apk` test
`panic_fixture_returns_typed_error_not_panic` feeds it to Eclipse's own reader and asserts a
typed `ApkError::Axml(..)` is returned (never a panic).

**Provenance (2026-06-04):** hand-crafted to trip the old parser's internal assertions;
contains no copyrighted content. Retained as the durable guard that the panic-on-hostile-AXML
root cause stays fixed.
